The arc length is $\int_0^{2\pi} |f'(\theta)|\,d\theta$. Since $f'(\theta) = ie^{i\theta}(1+e^{i\theta})^2$, we get $|f'(\theta)| = |1+e^{i\theta}|^2 = 2+2\cos\theta$, so the integral is $4\pi$.

Solution 1 reaches this value (its numerical final answer, 12.566…, equals $4\pi$), but its claim that the curve is simple is false. The points $z=e^{2\pi i/3}$ and $z=e^{-2\pi i/3}$ both map to $f=-2/3$, so the curve has a self-intersection. Solution 3 also reaches $4\pi$ in its work but ends with "Final answer: 4," which conflicts with its own derivation. Solution 2 likewise derives $4\pi$ but states "Final answer: 3."

Taking the perimeter of $R$ to be the total length of the boundary curve, which is the full curve traced once, the answer is $4\pi$. This reading is my interpretation of the problem; if $R$ meant only the inner loop between the self-intersection, the length would instead be $\frac{4\pi}{3}-2\sqrt{3}$, which matches none of the solutions.
